svg.aria-label: One circuit against exhaustive search, in three units. A 3x3 board with one solution, against 16,384 gate-steps for exhaustive search on one processor: 2^9 grids at the median cost of a whole-grid check over one-solution boards. Against the page's own backtracker the circuit loses in every unit: about 192 gate-steps at the median board, which its two-qubit count alone is 17x past. Width times depth charges the circuit for qubits it holds idle, and the classical side for no width at all, which is most of the spread here. FakeTorino (133 q, heavy-hex, basis cz/id/rz/sx/x), optimization level 3, qiskit 2.4.1. A fit to a device model, not a run on hardware. The oracle is written from the clues and compiled into one marked grid per solution, so every quantum figure is a lower bound.
